title: Morphexsynth

commands.name: SetVolume
commands.doc: Sets the level of the patch.

args.name: db
args.doc: level of the patch in dB (the Vol dial adds to it)

commands.name: SetOscillator
commands.doc: Sets one of the three oscillators.

fields.name: detune
fields.doc: tuning against the note in semitones

fields.name: pitchFactor
fields.doc: frequency factor against the note (2 is an octave up)

commands.name: SetFilterEnvelope
commands.doc: Sets the filter envelope and how far it moves the cutoff.

fields.name: contour
fields.doc: how far the envelope moves the cutoff (positive opens the filter as the envelope rises)

commands.name: SetPitchEnvelope
commands.doc: Sets the pitch envelope and the glide between notes.

fields.name: depthSemitones
fields.doc: how far the envelope bends the pitch in semitones

fields.name: glideMsPerOctave
fields.doc: glide time per octave from note to note in ms

commands.name: SetLfo
commands.doc: Sets the LFO of every voice.

fields.name: filterDepth
fields.doc: how far the LFO moves the cutoff

fields.name: oscDepth
fields.doc: pitch modulation of all three oscillators in semitones

fields.name: keyFollow
fields.doc: how much the note changes the LFO rate

commands.name: SetFilter
commands.doc: Sets the filter: cutoff, resonance and type.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: filter type, default LP4 (see Filter types below)

commands.name: SetCtrlSlot
commands.doc: Sets one slot of the routing matrix: it reads one source, shapes it by a curve, scales it by the depth and adds the result to a target.

args.name: slot
args.doc: which of the 10 routing slots, 0 to 9

fields.name: target
fields.doc: what the slot moves (None switches the slot off)

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: how far the slot moves the target

commands.name: SetMpeZone
commands.doc: Sets the MPE channels (1 to 16): master and the member channels lower to upper.

commands.name: SetPhaser
commands.doc: Sets the phaser of the effects bus.

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: how far the sweep spans 200 Hz to 2 kHz

commands.name: SetChorus
commands.doc: Sets the chorus of the effects bus.

commands.name: SetReverb
commands.doc: Sets the reverb of the effects bus.

fields.name: sizeMeters
fields.doc: size of the room in metres

fields.name: dryDb
fields.doc: level of the dry signal in dB

fields.name: mixDb
fields.doc: level of the reverb in dB (-100 is off)

commands.name: SetWaveMorph
commands.doc: Lets an oscillator morph between three waveforms: the one of SetOscillator, then waveform2 and waveform3. With morph = 0 (the default) the oscillator sounds exactly as without it; call it again from a hook to move the position while notes sound.

fields.name: waveform2
fields.doc: waveform of the second slot (default Square)

fields.name: waveform3
fields.doc: waveform of the third slot (default Saw)

fields.name: morph
fields.doc: position over the three slots: 0 the waveform of SetOscillator, 0.5 the second, 1 the third, between them a crossfade; a change takes 10 ms

hooks.name: OnStart
hooks.doc: Called once after the script is loaded; the usual place to set up a patch.

hooks.name: OnNoteOn
hooks.doc: A note began. channel counts from 0, velocity is 1 to 127.

hooks.name: OnNoteOff
hooks.doc: A note ended (a note on with velocity 0 counts as one).

hooks.name: OnPitchBend
hooks.doc: A pitch bend arrived, centred on 0 (-8192 to 8191).

enums.name: CtrlSource
enums.doc: What a routing slot reads (X: per-note pitch bend, Y: CC 74 and mod wheel, Z: pressure).

enums.name: CtrlCurve
enums.doc: Shape applied to the source before it is scaled.

enums.name: CtrlValueType
enums.doc: Abs: the source runs 0 to 1; BiPolar: it runs -1 to 1 around the middle.

examples.title: A patch in OnStart
examples.summary: The smallest useful patch: a saw through a lowpass filter with an amplitude envelope. Shows that a patch is a list of Set... commands in OnStart, and that what a script leaves out starts from a blank patch. Change the waveform (OscWaveform.Square ...), the cutoff (a note number) or the release.
examples.code:
-- A patch in OnStart
-- The smallest useful patch: a saw through a lowpass filter with an amplitude envelope. Shows that a patch is a list of
-- Set... commands in OnStart, and that what a script leaves out starts from a blank patch. Change the waveform
-- (OscWaveform.Square ...), the cutoff (a note number) or the release.
function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-6)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.6 })
    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 5, decayMs = 200, sustainLevel = 0.7, releaseMs = 250 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 80, resonance = 0.2, type = "LP4" })
end

examples.title: Mod wheel to the filter
examples.summary: The mod wheel (the Y source) opens the filter. Shows SetCtrlSlot: a slot reads a source, shapes it with a curve, scales it by the depth and adds it to a target. Start with the wheel down and a dark filter, then push it up. Change the target (CtrlTarget.Pan ...) or the depth.
examples.code:
-- Mod wheel to the filter
-- The mod wheel (the Y source) opens the filter. Shows SetCtrlSlot: a slot reads a source, shapes it with a curve,
-- scales it by the depth and adds it to a target. Start with the wheel down and a dark filter, then push it up. Change
-- the target (CtrlTarget.Pan ...) or the depth.
function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-6)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.6 })
    SetOscillator(1, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.4, detune = 0.12 })
    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 5, decayMs = 200, sustainLevel = 0.7, releaseMs = 250 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 40, resonance = 0.3 })
    SetCtrlSlot(0, {
        source = CtrlSource.Y,
        curve = CtrlCurve.Linear,
        target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
        valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs,
        depth = 0.8,
    })
end

examples.title: Pressure to resonance
examples.summary: Pressing a key harder (the Z source, channel or MPE pressure) raises the resonance, and the velocity of the key brightens the note. Shows two slots with different sources and value types: velocity 64 leaves the cutoff where it is (BiPolar), pressure starts at nothing (Abs). Change the depth to hear less or more.
examples.code:
-- Pressure to resonance
-- Pressing a key harder (the Z source, channel or MPE pressure) raises the resonance, and the velocity of the key
-- brightens the note. Shows two slots with different sources and value types: velocity 64 leaves the cutoff where it
-- is (BiPolar), pressure starts at nothing (Abs). Change the depth to hear less or more.
function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-6)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Square, level = 0.6, pwm = 0.2 })
    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 3, decayMs = 150, sustainLevel = 0.8, releaseMs = 150 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 60, resonance = 0.2 })
    SetCtrlSlot(0, {
        source = CtrlSource.Z,
        curve = CtrlCurve.SquareRoot,
        target = CtrlTarget.FilterResonance,
        valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs,
        depth = 0.6,
    })
    SetCtrlSlot(1, {
        source = CtrlSource.Velocity,
        curve = CtrlCurve.Linear,
        target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
        valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar,
        depth = 0.3,
    })
end

examples.title: An effects chain
examples.summary: A patch with the four effects of the effects bus: distortion, chorus, phaser and reverb. Shows that the effects are set like the rest of the patch, and that a mix of 0 (or -100 dB for the reverb) switches one off. Set the effects you do not want to their off values to hear each one on its own.
examples.code:
-- An effects chain
-- A patch with the four effects of the effects bus: distortion, chorus, phaser and reverb. Shows that the effects are
-- set like the rest of the patch, and that a mix of 0 (or -100 dB for the reverb) switches one off. Set the effects you
-- do not want to their off values to hear each one on its own.
function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-9)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.6 })
    SetOscillator(1, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.4, detune = 0.1 })
    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 10, decayMs = 300, sustainLevel = 0.6, releaseMs = 400 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 70, resonance = 0.15 })
    SetDistortion(2)
    SetChorus({ rateHz = 0.5, depth = 0.4, mix = 0.4 })
    SetPhaser({ rateHz = 0.2, depth = 0.5, feedback = 0.3, mix = 0.3 })
    SetReverb({ sizeMeters = 15, decayMs = 2000, dryDb = 0, mixDb = -12 })
end

examples.title: Vibrato with the LFO
examples.summary: A slow sine LFO moves the pitch of all oscillators by a quarter of a semitone each way, 5.5 times a second. Shows SetLfo: oscDepth is pitch in semitones, filterDepth moves the cutoff instead. Change speedHz and oscDepth, or move the depth to filterDepth for a wobble of the tone instead of the pitch.
examples.code:
-- Vibrato with the LFO
-- A slow sine LFO moves the pitch of all oscillators by a quarter of a semitone each way, 5.5 times a second. Shows
-- SetLfo: oscDepth is pitch in semitones, filterDepth moves the cutoff instead. Change speedHz and oscDepth, or move
-- the depth to filterDepth for a wobble of the tone instead of the pitch.
function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-6)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Triangle, level = 0.7 })
    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 30, decayMs = 200, sustainLevel = 0.8, releaseMs = 300 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 90, resonance = 0.1 })
    SetLfo({ waveform = LfoWaveform.Sine, speedHz = 5.5, oscDepth = 0.25, filterDepth = 0 })
end

examples.title: Patches by program change
examples.summary: Program change 0 gives a bright saw, 1 a dark square with a long release. Shows OnProgramChange and that the commands work from a hook too, not only in OnStart. Add a table entry for each patch.
examples.code:
-- Patches by program change
-- Program change 0 gives a bright saw, 1 a dark square with a long release. Shows OnProgramChange and that the
-- commands work from a hook too, not only in OnStart. Add a table entry for each patch.
local patches = {
    [0] = function()
        SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.6 })
        SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 3, decayMs = 150, sustainLevel = 0.7, releaseMs = 120 })
        SetFilter({ cutoff = 90, resonance = 0.2 })
    end,
    [1] = function()
        SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Square, level = 0.6, pwm = 0.3 })
        SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 40, decayMs = 400, sustainLevel = 0.6, releaseMs = 900 })
        SetFilter({ cutoff = 50, resonance = 0.3 })
    end,
}

function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-6)
    patches[0]()
end

function OnProgramChange(channel, program)
    local patch = patches[program]
    if patch then
        patch()
    end
end

examples.title: Wave morph on a controller
examples.summary: Controller 1 (the mod wheel) moves oscillator 0 from a triangle through a square to a saw. Shows SetWaveMorph called from OnCC while notes sound, and the value 0 to 127 scaled to 0 to 1. Change the controller number or the waveforms.
examples.code:
-- Wave morph on a controller
-- Controller 1 (the mod wheel) moves oscillator 0 from a triangle through a square to a saw. Shows SetWaveMorph called
-- from OnCC while notes sound, and the value 0 to 127 scaled to 0 to 1. Change the controller number or the waveforms.
function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-6)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Triangle, level = 0.7 })
    SetWaveMorph(0, { waveform2 = OscWaveform.Square, waveform3 = OscWaveform.Saw, morph = 0 })
    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 5, decayMs = 200, sustainLevel = 0.8, releaseMs = 250 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 90, resonance = 0.1 })
end

function OnCC(channel, controller, value)
    if controller == 1 then
        SetWaveMorph(0, { waveform2 = OscWaveform.Square, waveform3 = OscWaveform.Saw, morph = value / 127 })
    end
end

scripts.title: Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/4 Ever Mini.json); SetVolume is the
scripts.summary: level of the patch, a field of that file there. The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
scripts.code:
-- Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/4 Ever Mini.json); SetVolume is the
-- level of the patch, a field of that file there.
-- The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that
-- a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
import "constants"

function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-2.401)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = 3, level = 0.6786, pitchFactor = 0.5, pwm = 0.3 })
    SetOscillator(1, { waveform = 1, level = 0.7833, detune = -0.1724, pitchFactor = 0.5 })
    SetOscillator(2, { waveform = 4, level = 0.3108 })  -- noise

    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 2, decayMs = 9.89, sustainLevel = 1, releaseMs = 9.89 })
    SetFilterEnvelope({ attackMs = 41.39, decayMs = 374.1, sustainLevel = 0.2814, releaseMs = 374.1 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 54.49, resonance = 0.4807, type = "LP4" })

    -- Filter envelope has no cutoff path of its own yet (engine gap, see
    -- port-minimoog-presets.md Gap 2) - routed through the MPE matrix instead.
    SetCtrlSlot(0, { source = 5, curve = 2, target = 3, valueType = 0, depth = 0.4058 })

    -- osc3 is Minimoog's free-running pitch-wobble modulator (oscMod=1,
    -- filtModEnable=0), approximated via the LFO's oscDepth.
    SetLfo({ waveform = 1, speedHz = 1.461, oscDepth = 0.06829, keyFollow = 0 })

    -- X (pitch bend): standard +/-2 semitones
    SetCtrlSlot(1, { source = CtrlSource.X, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.PitchBend,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 2 / 12 })

    -- Z (pressure): aftertouch opens the filter
    SetCtrlSlot(2, { source = CtrlSource.Z, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.4 })

    -- Velocity: harder keys are brighter, soft ones darker (velocity 64 leaves the patch as it is)
    SetCtrlSlot(3, { source = CtrlSource.Velocity, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 0.3 })
end

scripts.title: Airy Pad: three detuned saws with a slow attack/release and a slow filter sweep,
scripts.summary: widened by the master chorus and set in space by the master reverb. The mod wheel (Y) opens the filter for a gentle brightening swell. Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Airy Pad.json); SetVolume is the level of the patch, a field of that file there. The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
scripts.code:
-- Airy Pad: three detuned saws with a slow attack/release and a slow filter sweep,
-- widened by the master chorus and set in space by the master reverb. The mod
-- wheel (Y) opens the filter for a gentle brightening swell.
-- Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Airy Pad.json); SetVolume is the
-- level of the patch, a field of that file there.
-- The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that
-- a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
import "constants"

function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-6.0)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.5, detune = 0.15, pitchFactor = 1.0 })
    SetOscillator(1, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.5, detune = -0.15, pitchFactor = 1.0 })
    SetOscillator(2, { waveform = OscWaveform.Triangle, level = 0.3, pitchFactor = 2.0 })

    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 800, decayMs = 400, sustainLevel = 0.8, releaseMs = 1200 })
    SetFilterEnvelope({ attackMs = 1500, decayMs = 500, sustainLevel = 0.7, releaseMs = 1000, contour = 1.6 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 66, resonance = 0.15, type = "LP4" })
    SetPitchEnvelope({ attackMs = 0, decayMs = 0, depthSemitones = 0, glideMsPerOctave = 0 })
    SetDistortion(0)

    -- filterDepth is semitones-ish; 0.5 swung the cutoff far too widely for a slow
    -- pad wash, so this is trimmed to a gentle drift.
    SetLfo({ waveform = LfoWaveform.Triangle, speedHz = 0.18, filterDepth = 0.125, oscDepth = 0, keyFollow = 0 })

    SetChorus({ rateHz = 0.5, depth = 0.6, mix = 0.6 })
    SetReverb({ sizeMeters = 24, decayMs = 3200, dryDb = 0, mixDb = -10 })
    SetPhaser({ rateHz = 0.15, depth = 0.6, feedback = 0.15, mix = 0.2 })

    -- Y (mod wheel / slide): slow additional brightening
    SetCtrlSlot(0, { source = CtrlSource.Y, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.7 })

    -- X (pitch bend): standard +/-2 semitones
    SetCtrlSlot(1, { source = CtrlSource.X, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.PitchBend,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 2 / 12 })

    -- Z (pressure): aftertouch opens the filter
    SetCtrlSlot(2, { source = CtrlSource.Z, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.4 })

    -- Velocity: harder keys are brighter, soft ones darker (velocity 64 leaves the patch as it is)
    SetCtrlSlot(3, { source = CtrlSource.Velocity, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 0.25 })
end

scripts.title: Crystal Bells: real bells ring with inharmonic partials, not a harmonic
scripts.summary: series - hum (an octave below the strike pitch), prime (the strike pitch), and tierce (a minor third above) dominate what's actually heard. The 3 oscillators cover those (mellow Triangle, not bright Square/Saw); high filter resonance adds a 4th, self-ringing partial on the strike, and a strong positive filter-envelope contour lets that brightness decay away as the bell mellows, rather than staying bright forever. Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Crystal Bells.json); SetVolume is the level of the patch, a field of that file there. The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
scripts.code:
-- Crystal Bells: real bells ring with inharmonic partials, not a harmonic
-- series - hum (an octave below the strike pitch), prime (the strike pitch),
-- and tierce (a minor third above) dominate what's actually heard. The 3
-- oscillators cover those (mellow Triangle, not bright Square/Saw); high
-- filter resonance adds a 4th, self-ringing partial on the strike, and a
-- strong positive filter-envelope contour lets that brightness decay away
-- as the bell mellows, rather than staying bright forever.
-- Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Crystal Bells.json); SetVolume is the
-- level of the patch, a field of that file there.
-- The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that
-- a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
import "constants"

function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-5.0)
    -- hum: an octave below the strike pitch, detuned for a slow natural beat
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Triangle, level = 0.55, detune = 0.04, pitchFactor = 0.5 })
    -- prime: the strike pitch itself
    SetOscillator(1, { waveform = OscWaveform.Triangle, level = 0.6, detune = -0.03, pitchFactor = 1.0 })
    -- tierce: a minor third above prime - the classic "bell" inharmonicity
    SetOscillator(2, { waveform = OscWaveform.Triangle, level = 0.35, pitchFactor = 1.2 })

    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 2, decayMs = 2200, sustainLevel = 0, releaseMs = 2200 })
    -- Bright at the strike, mellowing as it rings down: a fairly closed base
    -- cutoff, with a strong positive contour supplying the initial clang.
    SetFilterEnvelope({ attackMs = 2, decayMs = 900, sustainLevel = 0, releaseMs = 900, contour = 3.5 })
    -- Resonance held high (not self-oscillating) so the filter itself rings at
    -- its own cutoff on the strike transient - a cheap 4th, pitched partial.
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 62, resonance = 0.72, type = "LP4" })
    SetPitchEnvelope({ attackMs = 0, decayMs = 0, depthSemitones = 0, glideMsPerOctave = 0 })
    -- A struck bell has no ongoing vibrato.
    SetLfo({ waveform = LfoWaveform.Sine, speedHz = 3, filterDepth = 0, oscDepth = 0, keyFollow = 0 })
    SetDistortion(0)

    SetChorus({ rateHz = 0.7, depth = 0.3, mix = 0.25 })
    SetReverb({ sizeMeters = 30, decayMs = 4000, dryDb = 0, mixDb = -8 })
    SetPhaser({ rateHz = 0.25, depth = 0.4, feedback = 0.1, mix = 0.12 })

    -- X (pitch bend): standard +/-2 semitones, for the occasional bell glissando
    SetCtrlSlot(0, { source = CtrlSource.X, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.PitchBend,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 2 / 12 })

    -- Z (pressure): aftertouch makes the filter ring louder (the filter envelope has opened the cutoff already)
    SetCtrlSlot(1, { source = CtrlSource.Z, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterResonance,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.1 })

    -- Velocity: harder keys are brighter, soft ones darker (velocity 64 leaves the patch as it is)
    SetCtrlSlot(2, { source = CtrlSource.Velocity, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 0.5 })
end

scripts.title: Cutting Lead: two detuned unison saws through a bright, open filter, with a
scripts.summary: subtle always-on LFO vibrato. Z (pressure) and the mod wheel (Y) both brighten the filter for expressive lead lines; X bends a standard +/-2 semitones. Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Cutting Lead.json); SetVolume is the level of the patch, a field of that file there. The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
scripts.code:
-- Cutting Lead: two detuned unison saws through a bright, open filter, with a
-- subtle always-on LFO vibrato. Z (pressure) and the mod wheel (Y) both brighten
-- the filter for expressive lead lines; X bends a standard +/-2 semitones.
-- Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Cutting Lead.json); SetVolume is the
-- level of the patch, a field of that file there.
-- The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that
-- a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
import "constants"

function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-4.0)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.5, detune = 0.08, pitchFactor = 1.0 })
    SetOscillator(1, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.5, detune = -0.08, pitchFactor = 1.0 })
    -- A third, centered saw thickens the unison without pulling it off pitch.
    SetOscillator(2, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.4, detune = 0, pitchFactor = 1.0 })

    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 8, decayMs = 60, sustainLevel = 0.9, releaseMs = 150 })
    SetFilterEnvelope({ attackMs = 5, decayMs = 200, sustainLevel = 0.6, releaseMs = 150, contour = 1.2 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 92, resonance = 0.3, type = "LP4" })
    SetPitchEnvelope({ attackMs = 0, decayMs = 0, depthSemitones = 0, glideMsPerOctave = 0 })
    -- Subtle vibrato: oscDepth is semitones-ish, so keep this small - anything above
    -- ~0.02 reads as wobbly rather than a gentle, always-on vibrato.
    SetLfo({ waveform = LfoWaveform.Sine, speedHz = 5.2, filterDepth = 0, oscDepth = 0.02, keyFollow = 0 })
    SetDistortion(0)

    SetReverb({ sizeMeters = 14, decayMs = 1400, dryDb = 0, mixDb = -16 })
    SetChorus({ rateHz = 0.5, depth = 0.3, mix = 0.25 })
    SetPhaser({ rateHz = 0.3, depth = 0.5, feedback = 0.2, mix = 0.15 })

    -- Z (pressure): aftertouch brightening while a note is held
    SetCtrlSlot(0, { source = CtrlSource.Z, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.6 })
    -- Y (mod wheel / slide): brighten further
    SetCtrlSlot(1, { source = CtrlSource.Y, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.5 })
    -- X (pitch bend): standard +/-2 semitones
    SetCtrlSlot(2, { source = CtrlSource.X, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.PitchBend,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 2 / 12 })

    -- Z (pressure): aftertouch adds resonance
    SetCtrlSlot(3, { source = CtrlSource.Z, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterResonance,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.25 })

    -- Velocity: harder keys are brighter, soft ones darker (velocity 64 leaves the patch as it is)
    SetCtrlSlot(4, { source = CtrlSource.Velocity, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 0.3 })
end

scripts.title: Grand Stage: a triangle body with a touch of detuned saw edge for hammer
scripts.summary: brightness, a fast attack and a long natural decay rather than a held plateau. Velocity brightens the tone (harder hit = brighter), pressure opens the filter and the wheel bends; there is no vibrato, which does not suit this voicing. Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Grand Stage.json); SetVolume is the level of the patch, a field of that file there. The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.

-- Grand Stage: a triangle body with a touch of detuned saw edge for hammer
-- brightness, a fast attack and a long natural decay rather than a held plateau.
-- Velocity brightens the tone (harder hit = brighter), pressure opens the filter and the
-- wheel bends; there is no vibrato, which does not suit this voicing.
-- Factory patch of Morphexsynth, from AbacDsp (examples/morphexsynth/factory-patches/Grand Stage.json); SetVolume is the
-- level of the patch, a field of that file there.
-- The slots for pitch bend (X), pressure (Z) and velocity are this repository's addition to the AbacDsp patch, so that
-- a keyboard on channel 1 and an MPE controller both play it expressively.
import "constants"

function OnStart()
    SetVolume(-3.0)
    SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Triangle, level = 0.65, pitchFactor = 1.0 })
    SetOscillator(1, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.2, detune = 0.05, pitchFactor = 1.0 })
    -- A quiet octave-up layer, for extra harmonic complexity in the hammer strike.
    SetOscillator(2, { waveform = OscWaveform.Square, level = 0.1, pitchFactor = 2.0 })

    SetAmpEnvelope({ attackMs = 2, decayMs = 3500, sustainLevel = 0.15, releaseMs = 250 })
    SetFilterEnvelope({ attackMs = 2, decayMs = 2000, sustainLevel = 0.3, releaseMs = 250, contour = 0.8 })
    SetFilter({ cutoff = 88, resonance = 0.05, type = "LP4" })
    SetPitchEnvelope({ attackMs = 0, decayMs = 0, depthSemitones = 0, glideMsPerOctave = 0 })
    -- No vibrato - matches this voicing's own "deliberately static" design.
    SetLfo({ waveform = LfoWaveform.Sine, speedHz = 4, filterDepth = 0, oscDepth = 0, keyFollow = 0 })
    SetDistortion(0)

    -- A stage-piano's classic pedal chain: gentle room, a touch of tremolo-ish
    -- chorus and phaser for that electric-piano character.
    SetReverb({ sizeMeters = 18, decayMs = 2000, dryDb = 0, mixDb = -14 })
    SetChorus({ rateHz = 0.5, depth = 0.4, mix = 0.3 })
    SetPhaser({ rateHz = 0.25, depth = 0.4, feedback = 0.15, mix = 0.15 })

    -- Velocity: harder hits are brighter
    SetCtrlSlot(0, { source = CtrlSource.Velocity, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.6 })

    -- X (pitch bend): standard +/-2 semitones
    SetCtrlSlot(1, { source = CtrlSource.X, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.PitchBend,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.BiPolar, depth = 2 / 12 })

    -- Z (pressure): aftertouch opens the filter
    SetCtrlSlot(2, { source = CtrlSource.Z, curve = CtrlCurve.Linear, target = CtrlTarget.FilterCutoff,
                     valueType = CtrlValueType.Abs, depth = 0.4 })
end

guide:
# Writing a Morphexsynth script (guide for an AI assistant)

Morphexsynth is a polyphonic synthesizer with three oscillators, a filter, envelopes, an LFO, a routing matrix and an
effects bus. Its sound is a Lua script: a list of commands that set the patch, and hooks that react to MIDI. This file
tells you how to work here. It holds no names, ranges or limits of the API: those are in `API.md` and `constants.lua`
next to it, generated from the plugin, and always right. Read them first.

## 1. What a script is, and what is in this folder

- A script is one Lua 5.4 text file. Its top-level code and `OnStart` run once when it is loaded, and the commands they
  call (`SetOscillator`, `SetFilter`, `SetCtrlSlot`, ...) make **the patch**. The patch starts from a blank one
  (everything off, no oscillator sounding): a sound needs at least an oscillator with a level, and an amplitude
  envelope and a filter you can hear. What the script leaves out stays at the blank value.
- After that the plugin calls the hooks the script defines (`OnNoteOn`, `OnNoteOff`, `OnCC`, `OnProgramChange`,
  `OnPitchBend`). A hook that is not defined is not called. Commands called from a hook change the sound later, one at
  a time.
- Files here: `API.md` (every command, hook, constant and limit), `constants.lua` (the named constants such as
  `OscWaveform.Saw`, already global in every script), `examples/` (small patches that run as they are) and the ten
  factory patches (`warm-bass.lua`, `airy-pad.lua`, ...). The factory patches are read only: copy one to start from a
  complete sound.

## 2. Where a script goes

- On the Dwarf a script is a file `/data/jaypacks/scripts/morphexsynth/user-1.lua` up to `user-8.lua`. Reach it with
  `ssh root@192.168.51.1` and `scp -O`; the data partition survives a plugin update.
- Select it with the plugin's Script setting (User 1 to User 8). While a script is selected the Patch setting is ignored.
  To change a factory patch or an example, copy it to a user slot.
- A script may `import "name"` for another script file of the same folder; `io`, `os`, `require` and `load` do not exist.

## 3. The loop to follow

1. Write the script to a user slot.
2. The plugin checks the file twice a second and reloads it after a save. Nothing is restarted. The notes that sound are
   released and the new patch is loaded as a whole.
3. Read `/data/jaypacks/scripts/morphexsynth/user-1.log` (same name as the script, `.log`). It says whether the load
   worked, the message with the line of an error, the calls that were ignored, and every line the script wrote with
   `Log(...)`. The plugin's Script status output shows the same in a number (1 ok, 3 compile error, 4 runtime error,
   5 over the budget, 6 out of memory).
4. Play a note and listen. Fix what the log says, or what you hear, and save again.

A script that fails to load (syntax error, error at the top level or in `OnStart`) is rejected and the previous sound
goes on, so a typo never silences the synth; but the new script is not running either. Always read the log after a save.
An error in a hook ends only that call; the next event runs again.

## 4. Rules in short

- Hooks are global functions with fixed names and argument lists (`API.md`, Hooks). Write `function OnStart()`, not a local.
- Channels count from 0 in the hooks of this plugin (MIDI channel 1 is 0). Notes are 0 to 127, velocity 1 to 127, pitch
  bend -8192 to 8191, controller values 0 to 127.
- Commands take positional arguments (an index, a preset) and, last, an optional table of named fields:
  `SetOscillator(0, { waveform = OscWaveform.Saw, level = 0.6 })`. The three oscillators are 0 to 2, the routing slots
  0 to 9.
- Units: times are in milliseconds (`attackMs`), levels are 0 to 1 unless the API says otherwise, the volume is in dB,
  the filter cutoff is a note number (60 = middle C, up to 135), pitch depths are in semitones.
- A filter type is a text (`type = "LP4"`), not a constant; the names are listed in `API.md`.
- The routing matrix is how the player's hands reach the sound: a slot reads a source (X pitch bend, Y mod wheel, Z
  pressure, Velocity, Note, the envelopes), shapes it with a curve, scales it with the depth and adds it to a target
  (`CtrlSource`, `CtrlCurve`, `CtrlTarget`, `CtrlValueType` in `constants.lua`). A slot with the target `None` is off.
- Randomness is `math.random`; it gives the same numbers on every run. Keep state in locals at the top of the script.
- A hook has a small budget of instructions and milliseconds: no long loops.
- A number field outside its range is clamped. An integer argument (an oscillator index, a slot, a preset) outside its
  range, or not whole, makes the call ignored and is written to the log. A field name the command does not know is
  ignored and logged. A wrong type or a missing argument is an error.

## 5. Mistakes seen most

Each line is a message the plugin writes to the log, and the fix.

| Log says | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `SetOscillator: 'index' = 3 is outside 0..2, call ignored` | There are three oscillators, 0 to 2. |
| `SetCtrlSlot: 'slot' = 10 is outside 0..9, call ignored` | There are ten routing slots, 0 to 9. |
| `SetOscillator: unknown field 'wave' is ignored` | The field is `waveform`; take the names from `API.md`. |
| `SetFilter: unknown filter type 'LP5', call ignored` | A filter type is one of the texts listed in `API.md`. |
| `SetFilter: 'type' must be a string, not number` | Write the type as text in quotes: `type = "LP4"`. |
| `SetDistortion expects 1 argument(s) and got 0` | A command called without its arguments. |
| `SetFilter: the last argument must be a table of fields, not number` | Named fields go in braces: `SetFilter({ cutoff = 60 })`. |
| attempt to index a nil value (global 'OscWaveform') | A misspelt constant. Names are case sensitive. |
| the script sounds like the previous one | It was rejected at load; the log has the reason. |
| silence | No oscillator has a level, or the amplitude envelope sustains at 0, or the cutoff is too low. |
| a hook does nothing | The hook name is misspelt (`OnNoteOn`, not `onNoteOn`), or its channel test counts from 1. |
